soft_deny: Triggering CI: gh workflow run, gh run rerun, gh pr ready, or pushing a branch whose purpose is to fire gates. Consumes shared CI capacity and runner time. The user dispatches runs themselves.

Publishing to GitHub: gh issue create, gh pr create, gh pr comment, gh pr review, gh pr merge. The body must be drafted to a markdown file and explicitly approved first. A blanket 'go ahead' authorizes only the reversible parts, and never a batch of publishes chained together.
git add of paths the user did not stage, or git commit without an explicit ask in the current message. Commit exactly what is already staged.
git push, force-push, branch deletion, or rewriting published history.
Starting a long build, code-generation, or benchmark run. The user drives those; the machine and its licences are shared.
Starting a second long build, generation, or test run while one is already in flight.

hooks.command: jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_response.filePath' | { read -r f; case "$f" in *.py) d=$(dirname "$f"); while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do [ -x "$d/.venv/bin/ruff" ] && break; d=$(dirname "$d"); done; r="$d/.venv/bin/ruff"; [ -x "$r" ] || r=ruff; "$r" format "$f" && "$r" check --fix "$f";; esac; } 2>/dev/null || true
